tagline: Through Bill Monroe's home country and down to the Ohio.
intro: The trail starts at the Muhlenberg County line on US 62 and works through Ohio County by Hartford and Beaver Dam to Rosine, then north on KY 69 through Dundee and Fordsville to the Ohio River at Hawesville. From there US 60 and a few river roads run west through Lewisport and Maceo to Owensboro, and KY 56 goes on to the McLean County line.

Bill Monroe was born on a farm near Rosine, a town named for a poet's pen name. He grew up following his uncle Pendleton Vandiver to dances where Vandiver played the fiddle, and later put him in a song, "Uncle Pen". His band, the Blue Grass Boys, gave the music its name.

moments.title: Rosine
moments.text: On Friday nights from April to mid-December, musicians play bluegrass in the small general store and the barn next door, where a bronze disk remembers Monroe.

moments.title: Lewisport
moments.text: In the Pate House here Abraham Lincoln won his first case, as the defendant, charged with running a ferry across the Ohio without a license.

moments.title: Owensboro
moments.text: The Bluegrass Music Hall of Fame and Museum stands near the river at First and Frederica streets, in a city that also calls itself the Barbecue Capital of the World.

sources.label: Kentucky Transportation Cabinet, Kentucky State and National Scenic Byways and Highways
